overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the stipend discussion flowed naturally from the noticed hiring topic, and the chair lawfully limited public comment to exclude questions. Conflict-of-interest and job-description complaints were declined as outside the law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board discussed and approved a stipend at its November 15, 2017 meeting, a topic not listed in the posted notice, which covered only a proposed hire.
allegations.key_passage: While that specific action was not reflected in the notice, the discussion naturally flowed from the notice topic.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair barred him from asking the Board questions during the public comment period at the January 17, 2018 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We conclude that the Board acted within the limits of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant raised conflict-of-interest concerns and an alleged failure to post proper job descriptions, which the AG said are not Open Meeting Law issues.
allegations.key_passage: Additional allegations relating to conflicts of interest and failure to post proper job descriptions are not allegations of violations of the Open Meeting Law, thus we decline to review them.
